analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES Monday 2nd November: Semis selloff, credit in focus, positioning, MSFT raise, CAP wrap, TEF/Liberty restructure, TEF/Indra digital euro
key_insights: Semis sold off sharply on Friday after an earlier period of stabilisation, with volumes near the 20-day average and limited supply on the GS desk. Asian semi names are bouncing this morning, while EU semis are retesting local lows.

Last week's results suggest AI demand remains robust. Power availability, delivery costs and funding are the main pressure points. Elevated gross exposure and subdued risk appetite amid macro uncertainty are amplifying the selloff.

Credit is the key risk gauge. Google, Amazon and Meta have negative FCF and more than $3tn of forward commitments, which shifts attention from growth to how long funding needs last. Microsoft is self-funding but has just issued $25bn of debt.

Hyperscaler CDS is at record levels, Oracle CDS is around 288bp, and S&P has a negative outlook on Meta (AA- rating maintained). Amazon's $80bn secured hardware facility and growing use of leases point to structures that protect liquidity and ratings.
Power limits near-term deployment, but credit stress could ultimately force a pause in capex. OpenAI's $10bn reduction in its raise and soft close weaken the offtake narrative supporting Oracle.

The GS software team's recurring client question is how much financing still needs to be raised for the datacenter build-out and whether the credit market is deep enough. Its work suggests the financing needed may be less than investors expect, the market can still absorb new IG issuance, and enterprise token demand may step up again in 2027.

Positioning: de-grossing continued for a third week despite net buying and above-average turnover. Gross exposure still looks high given unresolved Middle East tensions and this week's midterms. Lower gross exposure and normalising volatility are prerequisites for re-engagement.

Hedge fund performance: Systematic L/S fell 2.5% on the week, its worst since December 2023, and lost 3.6% in October. Fundamental L/S gained 0.3% on the week, but October was -3.5%. TMT funds lost 11.9% in October.
Among the top 10 weekly changes in GS TMT short positions, Adyen shorts rose 36% while CAP and IFX were among the decreases.

Virgin Media O2 is reportedly finalising a wholesale deal to use BT's Openreach network and freezing its own cable-to-fibre upgrades. It is also reportedly planning to cut 25% of its 16,000 workforce to address a £22bn debt pile. Regulatory opposition to the £2bn Nexfibre transaction threatens a planned £1.1bn cash injection.

NVIDIA reportedly cut Vera Rubin per-GPU HBM4 bandwidth by 13% and NVLink bandwidth by 17% on shipping specs, with compute unchanged. GS reads it as a HBM/yield or power constraint rather than a demand issue.

Microsoft priced a $25B multi-tranche bond, its first USD deal since 2017. It is the only large hyperscaler with positive quarterly FCF ($18.6B), so even the strongest balance sheet is financing externally. Its 5Y CDS has widened but remains the tightest in the group.
OpenAI reportedly cut its fundraising target to about $20B from $30B and its valuation to $1.25T from $1.4T.

Capgemini's 3Q26 delivered a third straight quarter of mid-single-digit organic growth. FY26 organic guidance rose for a second time, and GS raised its forecast to 4.4% from 4.1%. GS says the c.40% discount to Accenture looks increasingly unwarranted. Buy rating maintained.

Kioxia fell 14% after current-quarter operating profit guidance missed estimates despite strong NAND demand. Prices are agreed for only about half of sales volumes and a higher smart-device mix limits growth.
South Korea's October exports showed record DRAM exports of US$34bn. Memory exports are up 359% y/y, the ninth straight month above 200%, and WFE equipment exports are up 197% y/y.
CXMT's 3Q26 operating profit rose 23% q/q to 29% above GS estimates on better mix and higher DRAM prices. GS expects 4Q26 revenue up 4% q/q with gross margin at 86%.
MediaTek guided 4Q26 revenue sharply higher on its first AI accelerator shipments and raised its 2026 cloud ASIC revenue outlook to US$2.5bn. It confirmed a second ASIC customer.
Hon Hai guided double-digit growth in 2027 on AI infrastructure. It expects its AI-server market share to reach about 45% next year.

US trading: asset managers were net sellers on the week and hedge fund flows were balanced. Supply was concentrated in tech and looked systematic or top-down, with ETFs about 31% of the tape. Consumer outperformed on Thursday and Friday as money rotated from tech into staples.

Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers in macro products. Megacap tech was net sold in 4 of the last 5 sessions, which suggests little recovery in risk appetite.

Prediction markets imply a Democratic House win above 90% and a Senate win above 65%. GS expects no major fiscal policy change over two years, though spending could rise and the debt limit will need to be raised.
DoorDash said third-party AI agents have generated only several hundred orders in total, against about 3 million deliveries a day in 2025.
GS's AI adoption tracker rose 0.8% to 24.6% of US establishments, with adoption expected at 28.6% in six months.

The ECB selected Telefonica and Indra's Minsait to build and operate secure communications infrastructure for the planned digital euro. A Nokia software bug caused an outage of up to nine hours on Orange's French mobile network, and Orange is seeking compensation.
France's National Assembly narrowly approved an amendment to the 2027 budget proposing a 5.5-cent-per-GB tax on internet traffic aimed at large streaming platforms, estimated to raise about €5bn.

market_movers.rationale: Capgemini delivered a third straight quarter of mid-single-digit organic growth and raised FY26 guidance for a second time. GS sees the c.40% discount to Accenture as increasingly unwarranted.

sector_views.rationale: AI demand looks robust, but elevated gross exposure and subdued risk appetite are amplifying the selloff. Re-engagement needs lower gross exposure and normalising volatility.
Capgemini's growth outperformance supports a re-rating if organic growth, WNS synergies and margin resilience hold. Agentic AI remains a long-term risk.

earnings_insights: Capgemini 3Q26 reported: third consecutive quarter of mid-single-digit organic growth. FY26 organic growth guidance raised to 4-4.5% from 3.5-4%, implying c.2-3% in Q4. GS FY26 organic growth forecast raised to 4.4% from 4.1%.

Kioxia guidance: current-quarter operating profit guided at ¥2tn ($12.7bn) versus consensus estimate of ¥2.35tn, a miss. September-quarter selling prices rose a mid-20% rate versus 70% in the prior quarter, and bit shipments grew a low-teens percentage versus guidance of high-single-digit to 10%.

CXMT 3Q26 reported: gross margin 90% versus 88% in 2Q26, operating expenses 4.7% of revenue versus 5.4%, operating profit up 23% q/q and 29% above GS estimates. GS estimate for 4Q26: revenue +4% q/q, gross margin 86%.

MediaTek guidance: 4Q26 revenue NT$210-222bn (+25-32% q/q, +40-48% y/y), 2026 cloud ASIC revenue outlook raised to US$2.5bn, 2027 datacenter revenue seen at the upper end of the prior range (about US$16bn).
Hon Hai guidance: double-digit growth in 2027, weekly AI-rack output about 2,000 units, AI infrastructure 40-50% of revenue within 3-5 years.
DoorDash 3Q reported call commentary: third-party AI agents generated only several hundred orders in total.
Upcoming this week: Apple (tonight), AMD and Palantir report. European telcos DT, Swisscom, TI, BT and Cellnex also report, plus WKL in media.
Last week's reported results from CMG, WING, EAT, NCLH and RCL were better and supported consumer outperformance.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fiscal deadlines such as spending authority extension and a debt limit increase become the focus. GS expects no major fiscal policy change over two years, though spending could rise.
The election could also shape the outlook for AI regulation.

macro_indicators.indicator: GS AI adoption tracker, US establishments
macro_indicators.interpretation: Adoption is approaching 50% in the information, professional and finance sectors.
Memory exports are up 359% y/y, the ninth straight month above 200%, which supports the memory pricing and demand picture.

risk_factors: Credit stress from negative FCF and more than $3tn of forward commitments at hyperscalers could force a pause in capex.
Power availability, delivery costs and funding constrain AI deployment.
Elevated gross exposure combined with subdued risk appetite can amplify selloffs.
OpenAI's reduced raise and soft close weaken the offtake narrative supporting Oracle.
Agentic AI is a long-term risk to IT services.
Virgin Media O2 faces a £22bn debt pile, possible liability management and a potential block of the Nexfibre transaction.
Nokia software reliability is under scrutiny after the Orange outage.
A French per-GB traffic tax could be passed on to consumers through higher subscription prices.
vol_and_positioning: De-grossing continued for a third week despite net buying and above-average weekly turnover. Lower gross exposure and normalising volatility are prerequisites for re-engagement.

Systematic L/S fell 2.5% on the week and 3.6% in October. Fundamental L/S gained 0.3% on the week and is -3.5% for October. Asia-focused funds lost 9.5% in October. TMT funds fell 3.1% on the week and are -11.9% for October.
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 0.1 pts to 216.3% (66th percentile one-year). Net leverage rose 3.6 pts to 47% (7th percentile one-year).

Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers in macro products and to a lesser extent single stocks. Info Tech was the most net bought sector through Thursday but is still heavily net sold month to date.
Adyen shorts rose 36% on the week, among the top 10 weekly changes in GS TMT short positions by market value. CAP and IFX shorts were among the decreases.
ETFs were about 31% of the tape on Friday, the highest full-session level since June.
S&P key levels: 100-day moving average at 7614 and the CTA medium-term threshold at 7554, where most notional sits.
Covering in under-owned pockets such as CROX and BOOT helped consumer outperform on Thursday and Friday.
geopolitical: Unresolved Middle East tensions are cited as a reason gross exposure still looks high.
US midterm elections this week could determine the outlook for AI regulation and fiscal deadlines.
France's National Assembly approved an amendment for a per-GB tax on internet traffic aimed at large streaming platforms.
The ECB selected Telefonica and Indra's Minsait to build secure communications infrastructure for the planned digital euro.
